svg.title: Where each stage's beat goes (measured)
svg.desc: Each bar is one stage's time per beat: forward, host gap and waiting for upstream input add up to the beat. Left: lockstep vs decoupled on the same nodes; right: decoupled vs push + split on another set of nodes. Axes start at 0.
svg.text: Each bar = forward + host gap + waiting for upstream input = the beat, so a shorter bar is faster; dashed lines mark each arm's beat.
Each side ran back to back on one set of nodes (left 300 s each, right 1200 s each).
host gap (host thread waits on a rendezvous / sync)
One beat = forward + host gap + upstream wait (ms)

svg.text: • Every stage's host gap fell from 7-11 ms to under 1 ms; that is where the
• Idle per beat fell from 11-49 ms to 1-36 ms (bottom row).
• The forward segment grows a little: activations still go over NCCL, whose
receive kernel waits on the GPU, so the wait is counted as forward
(clearest on PP7, whose upstream wait moved almost entirely inside).
• On the right the gain is in the forward segment, not in idle time: NCCL
hides its waiting inside the forward, so the NCCL arm looks less idle. Push
no longer holds SMs while waiting: PP1-PP4 forward drops 5-28 ms; the
per-GPU split moves a layer off PP4, which sits on the slowest GPU.
• The remaining upstream waits come from unequal stage costs (about 6% from
